summary.text: A four-month-old intact male Bernese Mountain Dog weighing 20.8 kg was presented for orthopedic examination with an abnormal hind limb gait and gradually worsening right tarsal hyperextension for 2 weeks. Palpation of the lumbosacral region elicited pain, the hind limb gait was mildly stiff and a bit wide, and tarsal hyperextension and mild metatarsal outward rotation were found. The dog had no previous infections or predisposing illnesses.

Sedated radiographs showed erosive lesions of the left sacroiliac joint and mild hip laxity, and CT showed cystoid and concave defects with deep peripheral sclerosis of both joints, severe on the left and moderate on the right, with asymmetric widening of the joint spaces. The presumptive diagnosis was inflammatory and infectious sacroiliitis; degenerative and neoplastic disease were considered less likely.

The dog received carprofen 4 mg/kg SID for 3 weeks, physiotherapy, joint nutraceuticals and exercise restriction. Joint sampling and pelvic surgeries were declined by the owner. At the recheck after 3 weeks the dog was not lame and had no pain on palpation, and carprofen 2 mg/kg once daily was given for one more week; after a month the dog was clinically normal. Recheck radiographs after 6 weeks showed reduced erosive changes, with incomplete resolution.

At 1.5 years the owner reported normal activity without clinical complaints, palpation was non-painful, and radiographs and CT showed no evidence of erosive or sclerotic lesions. Hip screening classified the hips as D/D (moderate hip dysplasia) and conservative treatment with physiotherapy was elected. Non-septic erosive sacroiliitis was presumed; infection was not definitively excluded because joint aspiration and culture were not performed.

article_limitations: Single canine case report. SIJ aspiration and culture were not performed, so septic sacroiliitis is not definitively excluded and the diagnosis is presumed.

Normality after a month and at 6 weeks is consistent and accepted.
